title: Implementing OpenMP Offload Support in the AMD Next Generation Fortran Compiler
problem: Fortran remains dominant in HPC but classic Flang compiler limiting; modern supercomputers use GPUs (heterogeneous), requiring OpenMP offload support for GPU targeting; missing compiler support hinders Fortran adoption on GPU-accelerated systems.
motivation: Fortran has large HPC developer base and new high-performance code written daily. OpenMP is standard multithreading and GPU offload interface. AMD needs modernized Fortran compiler (AMD Flang replacing Classic Flang in ROCm 7.0) supporting GPU offload to enable Fortran on GPU-accelerated supercomputers.
method: AMD Flang implements OpenMP target directives—special code annotations that tell the compiler which Fortran code sections to run on GPUs. It uses map clauses to specify which data must be transferred to GPU memory. The compiler transforms Fortran code through multiple processing stages: converting it to an internal representation, handling loop constructs like DO CONCURRENT through the OpenMP intermediate representation, and generating GPU machine instructions.
key_novelty: AMD Flang adds GPU offload support to Fortran using OpenMP target directives.
contributions: AMD Next Generation Fortran Compiler (AMD Flang) with OpenMP offload support
OpenMP target directive and map clause implementation for GPU offloading
Compilation pipeline for heterogeneous GPU-accelerated systems
IR transformations enabling idiomatic Fortran constructs (DO CONCURRENT) on GPUs
